findings.element: .b-inert ("NOTHING TO PREVIEW YET", "SENDING COMES NEXT") and .b-who on the publish screen ("WHAT LANDS IN THE MESSAGE", "THE LINK")
findings.problem:
b.css:1296 declares the round-6 fix in its own words: "Uppercase mono is now exclusive to SECTION HEADS... state and provenance sit one ink step behind it" in sentence case at the data letterfit. Two categories still break it. (a) .b-inert is a STATE and renders 11px Geist Mono / lead 1.4 / 0.16em / uppercase / 62% - byte-identical to .b-measureHead, .b-behindLabel, .b-todayLabel and .b-label. On owner-empty it sits top-right, exactly where Preview and Publish live on the flight state, so the reader is handed a section head where a control was. (b) .b-who is the ceremonial 12px/0.20em step that shell.css:56 documents as "the ceremonial top line, and only that"; on publish it is emitted twice as a

for column captions (render-b.js:1341, :1348) while the couple's name is emitted as an

at the same 12px/0.20em/uppercase - and b.css:62 drops those captions to fore-62, which is precisely the ink .b-ogWho ("MARA & FINN", inside the card, on the same screen) already uses. On the one screen where the couple's name and the machine's captions appear together, all three are one typographic object with nothing at all separating them. Driven at 1440/1280/1152/768/390; both gates pass throughout, because the audit keys leading and tracking on family|size|role and every one of these derives to role "label".
findings.fix: Give state its own row in the sub-15 tier using ladders that already exist. Add .b-inert to the b.css:1304 override list (text-transform:none; letter-spacing:var(--track-data); color:var(--fore-62)) so "Nothing to preview yet" and "Sending comes next" read as sentence-case provenance rather than heads. Then split .b-who: keep --size-labelWide / --track-labelWide / --fore for the h1 identity line only, and give the publish captions a new selector .b-pressCap at --size-label / --lead-label / --track-label / --fore-62 - the section-head spec they actually are - replacing h("p.b-who") at render-b.js:1341 and :1348. No new size, weight, family or hue.

findings.element: .b-unit and .b-gapNote in the print sheet's left column
findings.problem: On screen .b-unit sits on the count's baseline exactly - measured true baselines at 1440 owner-flight: .b-num 386.69, .b-unit 386.69. On the printed keepsake the same pair reads .b-num 264.19 / .b-unit 294.97: the unit has left the figure's baseline by 31px and hangs 21px below the bottom of the 148px numeral. It is also given an 84px slot, so "days away on Thursday 16 July 2026" sets as three lines with line widths 84 / 56 / 84 - long, short, long, with "Thursday" orphaned alone on the middle line. Directly beneath it .b-gapNote is set at 15px inside a 220px box and breaks to "Nothing is planned" / "until 1 August." at 125px and 92px of used width - roughly a 17-character measure, well under any floor for 15px prose, and one comfortable line on every screen state. This is the artifact that gets framed, and it is the only state where the type loses an alignment the screen already holds.
findings.fix: In the print block, lock the unit to the count's baseline and to at most two lines: emit .b-unit as two spans - "days away on" and the date - with the date span carrying white-space:nowrap, widen its slot from 84px to at least 190px so the rag becomes two even lines, and keep the row on align-items:baseline so its first baseline matches .b-num as it does on screen. Raise the print left column from 220px to at least 300px (about 34ch at 15px) so .b-gapNote holds the same measure floor the rest of the system holds.

findings.problem: Driven at 390/420/480/560/640/700/767/768/900/1024/1152/1279/1280/1440/1600, every type size is identical from 390 to 766 and every one of them jumps at 767: .b-title 17 to 24 (+41%), .b-num 96 to 148 (+54%), .b-when 20 to 30 (+50%), .b-away 15 to 17. That is a 376px band - the widest single stretch in the responsive range - in which the ramp does not move at all while the content column grows from 350px to about 660px. At 700px the hero count is still at the phone's 96px inside a 660px column and the moment title is 17px inside a 470px box; the screen reads as a phone screenshot enlarged rather than a page laid out for its width. The declared typeRamp carries 20, 24, 30 and 48 steps that this band never uses, and one breakpoint is doing all the work for four objects at once.
findings.fix: Add one intermediate breakpoint at 560px (or a clamp() between the two anchors) that steps .b-num 96 to 120px, .b-when 20 to 24px (--size-head), .b-title 17 to 20px, .b-away 15 to 17px. All four values are already on ladders.typeRamp, so the measured gate stays clean; only the media query is new.

findings.problem: Driven by opening the editor from the row at 1440: the row renders the owner's words at 24px / 600 / lead 1.2 / -0.03em in a 544px box, and the field they type them into renders the same string at 17px / 400 / lead 1.4 / -0.015em in a 310px box. The person's own words shrink by seven points, drop a weight and change leading at the exact moment they are being written, then grow back on commit. It also means the field's measure (about 36ch) has no relation to the row's (about 45ch), so the owner cannot see where their title will actually break - which matters, because .b-title is clamped to two lines and the word-safe trim fires on the row, never in the field. The lessons library's rule is that a person's words get the larger, denser type wherever they sit beside metadata; here they get the smaller, lighter type in the one place the person is authoring them.
findings.fix: Set #b-edit-title to font-size:var(--size-date); font-weight:600; line-height:var(--lead-head); letter-spacing:var(--track-head) at 768 and above, and font-size:var(--size-lead); font-weight:600; line-height:var(--lead-head) at 390, so the field carries the row's weight, leading and letterfit at the panel's width. Keep the field's existing padding and height reserve; only the type changes.

findings.problem: Three break faults, none of which either gate can see. (a) .b-unfurlTitle carries no wrap policy (computed text-wrap: wrap) and at both 1280 and 1440 sets "Wedding day, Saturday" / "3 October 2026" - the break falls inside the date, between the weekday and the day-number, on the preview of the card that is the product's first impression inside a message. (b) .b-stepRead sets a full sentence in the code face and breaks it at 390, 1280 and 1440 as "Saturday 8 August 2026" / "in 23 days" with the middot leading the second line; a connector must never begin a line. (c) .b-emptyBody, .b-pressBody and .b-endedBody are two- and three-line leads carrying text-wrap:pretty, which only suppresses widows and never equalises, so they rag 381/226, 481/220 and 326/140 at every width above 390 - and at 390 .b-pressBody still widows "no prices." onto a third line at 22% of the measure, the only widow found in the entire twelve-state by six-width matrix.
findings.fix: (a) In render-b.js emit the unfurl title as two spans, "Wedding day," and the date, with the date span carrying white-space:nowrap, so the break lands after the comma. (b) Emit .b-stepRead's tail as its own span with white-space:nowrap and bind the middot to it with a non-breaking space, so the connector cannot start a line. (c) Change text-wrap:pretty to text-wrap:balance on .b-emptyBody (b.css:864), .b-pressBody, .b-endedBody and the print .b-gapNote - every one of them is four lines or fewer, which is exactly where balance applies.

biggestWin: The ladder is real, declared and honoured, and the hardest part of it is finished. Across twelve states and six widths the whole product resolves to twenty-seven distinct type settings in two families at two weights, on a tracking curve that runs +0.20em at the 12px ceremonial line down through 0.16 / 0.04 / -0.015 / -0.03 / -0.035 to -0.05em at 148px, and a leading curve of 1.5 / 1.4 / 1.3 / 1.2 / 1.06 / 0.9 bound to role rather than to size - so a 17px moment title and a 17px paragraph are correctly two different objects rather than one. On top of that the hero figure is optically corrected: .b-num carries a negative left margin that lands the ink of "79" at 186.6 against a label column at 186.0 at 148px, and at 20.2 against 20.0 at 96px, on screen and on paper, with the unit sitting on the figure's exact baseline. Measure is capped everywhere (34 to 52ch, nothing over 78ch at any width), figures are tabular on every counting object, trims are word-safe with the full string kept in the accessibility tree, and exactly one widow exists in the whole matrix. That is the part most teams never reach, and here it is already done.
